title: Florida House, District 89
what_it_does: Represents District 89 (Part of Palm Beach) in the Florida House; votes on state laws and the state budget.
verified_ballot_note: Candidate list taken from the Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list on 2026-09-18 (https://dos.elections.myflorida.com/candidates/CanList.asp); statuses Qualified/Unopposed only. Counties from the Legislature's district listings. Positions have not been researched yet.

candidates.name: Cathy Higgins
candidates.occupation: Co-owner of two local businesses; former Mayor and council member, City of Atlantis
candidates.background: Cathy Higgins was born in West Palm Beach and raised in Lake Worth. She served 12 years on the Atlantis City Council, three of them as the city's first woman mayor, and she and her husband run two local businesses that employ close to 400 people. She built a dance program at The King's Academy and won the August 2026 Republican primary with about 67 percent.

candidates.name: Debra Tendrich
candidates.photo_source: Ballotpedia candidate photo (downloaded copy in assets/photos)
candidates.occupation: Nonprofit founder and executive director; state representative since 2024
candidates.background: Debra Tendrich of Lake Worth is the founder and executive director of a nutrition-focused nonprofit and was elected to the Florida House in November 2024. In her first term she was the prime author of a domestic-violence protections law that passed both chambers unanimously, and she serves on the House Select Committee on Property Taxes.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

property_tax.summary: Voted no on HJR 1-F (June 2, 2026 special session), which put a $250,000 non-school homestead exemption on the November 2026 ballot, and no on HJR 203 (Feb. 19, 2026), which would have phased out non-school homestead property taxes.

sources.title: Florida House floor vote, CS/HJR 1-F (Save our Homes from Excessive Property Taxes), third reading

immigration.summary: Voted no on SB 2-C (Feb. 13, 2025), which created a State Board of Immigration Enforcement, funded state cooperation with federal immigration enforcement and added criminal penalties tied to immigration status.

sources.title: Florida House floor vote, SB 2-C (Immigration), 2025 Special Session C, third reading
Florida House roll call, SB 2-C passage (Yeas 85, Nays 30)
